title: Commit-or-Undo optimizer SDK gateway
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Optimize's recommendation engine must apply batching/caching suggestions safely to customer configs without risking double-apply, partial-apply, or invisible rollbacks. Current integration proofs-of-concept are brittle: retries can cause duplicate side-effects and operator recovery is manual.

Goal: Build an SDK+API gateway that provides transactional commit-or-undo semantics for Optimize recommendations. The gateway exposes a small REST surface for proposal lifecycle (create -> validate -> dry-run -> commit -> undo), accepts idempotency tokens for exactly-once intent, emits structured webhooks for downstream systems, and integrates with control-plane audit logs. The gateway must support dry-run (simulated cost delta), reconciliation hooks, and safe automatic rollback on failure windows.

High-level design:
- API endpoints: /proposals (POST), /proposals/{id}/validate (POST), /proposals/{id}/dry-run (POST), /proposals/{id}/commit (POST), /proposals/{id}/undo (POST), /proposals/{id}/status (GET).
- SDK primitives: ProposalBuilder, ProposalClient.commit(idempotency_key), ProposalClient.undo(idempotency_key), reconcile() helper. SDK will surface retry-safe helpers and optional optimistic locking.
- Idempotency model: Clients supply an idempotency_key (UUID v4) for any non-idempotent operation (commit/undo). The gateway stores canonical operation records with status {pending, applying, applied, undoing, undone, failed}. Duplicate requests with the same idempotency_key are deduped and return the canonical result or current state.
- Transactional behavior: Each commit is an orchestrated two-phase operation: (1) prepare changes and compute change-set + inverse operations (stored as an undo plan), (2) apply changes across the control plane via safe write APIs with per-resource retries and per-change acknowledgement. If any change fails irrecoverably within the predefined window, the gateway triggers the undo plan automatically and emits failure telemetry.
- Webhooks: Structured events for lifecycle transitions (proposal.created, proposal.validated, proposal.dry_run.complete, proposal.commit.started, proposal.commit.complete, proposal.undo.started, proposal.undo.complete, proposal.failed). Webhooks include the proposal id, idempotency_key, affected resources, cost_estimate_before, cost_estimate_after, and a rollover token for fetching logs. Delivery is retryable and ordered per-proposal.
- Observability: Emit metrics for commit latency, rollback rate, duplicate-idempotency attempts, and dry-run vs commit delta. Provide audit logs with operator identity, SDK client version, and request traces.
- Safety controls: configurable automatic rollback window, max retry attempts, per-customer rate limits, and a canary mode that applies to a fraction of resources for initial rollouts.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: UI/Console integration (console work ticket will be created), Dedicated-specific network packaging, and on-prem sidecar placement.

Acceptance criteria:
- API endpoints defined and implemented with OpenAPI spec checked into repo.
- SDK (python + typescript) implements ProposalClient.commit/undo with idempotency semantics and unit tests simulating retries.
- Gateway persists operation records and undo plans to the control-plane store with audit metadata.
- Automatic rollback triggers on simulated failure in integration tests and leaves system in pre-commit state.
- Webhook contract implemented and example consumer (mock) that proves ordered delivery and dedup handling.
- Integration smoke tests in CI that cover happy-path commit, duplicate commit with same idempotency_key, and commit->fail->automatic-undo flow.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We will favor a lightweight coordinator service over complex distributed transactions. The coordinator will use per-change idempotent apply operations offered by existing control-plane APIs where possible. Where the control-plane does not expose idempotent writes, the gateway will write compensating undo actions.
- Storing full undo plans increases storage but simplifies recovery; undo plans will be TTL'd after 30 days and archived to long-term logs.
- To avoid long blocking commits, large cross-resource proposals can opt into an asynchronous commit mode where commit returns a 202 and progress is polled via /status or delivered via webhooks.
- For replay safety we will include operation sequence numbers and sha256 hashes of the proposal payload in stored records.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Commit-or-Undo+Gateway (WIP)
- OpenAPI spec (PR): https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/1482
- Spike notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1x-example-spike
- Monitoring dashboard (temp): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/optimize/commit-gateway
- Example mock consumer for webhooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/tree/main/tests/mock-webhook-consumer

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Control-plane APIs are not idempotent and make undo plans complex. Mitigation: prioritize wrapping or enhancing control-plane APIs with idempotent primitives (follow-up ticket).
- Risk: Automatic undo could cascade failures. Mitigation: constrained automatic rollback window and canary gating; send operator alerts and provide manual override.
- Risk: Webhook consumers mishandle duplicates. Mitigation: include event_id + idempotency_key and best-practice consumer docs; provide retry backoff headers.

Next steps:
- Finalize OpenAPI and SDK prototypes (owner: Ravi).
- Create console surface ticket for rollout visualization (PM: Lina Zhou).
- Begin integration tests and add chaos scenarios to CI.
